The patient presents with a 10-year history of bilateral wrist and knee pain, accompanied by ~50 minutes of morning stiffness — consistent with inflammatory joint disease but falling short of the classic >30–60 minute duration often seen in rheumatoid arthritis (RA). Notably, there is *no* reported joint swelling, warmth, redness, systemic symptoms (fatigue, fever, weight loss, rash), or elevated acute-phase reactants beyond a mildly elevated ESR (10 mm/hr; normal typically <20 mm/hr for women, <15 for men — context-dependent), while CRP is normal. RF is negative (8 IU/mL, well below typical cutoffs of ~14–20 IU/mL).
